 Alexander Coolidge

Cincinnati Enquirer

Aug. 12, 2026, 12:30 a.m. ET

- Total Quality Logistics expects annual sales to surpass $10 billion, driven by AI and data center growth.
- The company's co-CEO credits a Trump administration immigration crackdown with tightening trucking capacity and increasing rates.
- TQL has expanded with its first international office in Mexico and plans to hire over 1,000 new employees nationwide.

The Union Township-based freight broker, which ships everything from groceries to rockets, expects its annual sales to climb above $10 billion for 2026, an increase of about a third, co-CEO Kerry Byrne told The Enquirer.

“AI is big: We are moving a lot of equipment to build those facilities and to equip them with tech that is needed. That is the hottest area right now,” Byrne said in an interview.

Maersk, the global integrator of container logistics operating across more than 130 countries, is deepening its footprint in North American contract logistics with a US$100m investment in a new fulfillment center in Hopedale, Massachusetts. The 617,000-square-foot facility is scheduled to open in late August 2026, positioning the company to strengthen fulfillment capacity for cargo owners across the region.

Built around the requirements of a single major e-commerce customer, the site will function as a central node in Maersk’s contract logistics network throughout the US Northeast. During peak periods, the center is engineered to process up to 330,000 units a day, a throughput enabled by advanced conveyor and sortation systems designed for high-volume, rapid-turnaround operations.

MyFreightWorld Expands in West Palm Beach, Adding 41 Jobs

# National Logistics Company to Expand West Palm Beach Operations

August 26, 2026 – West Palm Beach, FL – The Business Development Board of the Palm Beaches today announced the expansion of MyFreightWorld, a national third-party logistics company in West Palm Beach. The company will add 41 new team members over the next few years at an average income of $94,000. MyFreightWorld will move from its current location at 400 Clematis Street, Suite 203, into a 7,296-square-foot suite at 2090 Palm Beach Lakes Boulevard in West Palm Beach. The larger space is designed to support the company’s rapid growth and increased shipment activity across Palm Beach County and the country where it currently manages 25,000 shipments annually.

As it grows its current workforce from 20 to a total of 61 employees, the new positions are primarily for Account Executives and Account Management. Palm Beach County residents can apply online.

About the Expansion:

- Jobs: 41 new jobs in West Palm Beach; 20 current employees
- Pay: $94,000 average income

## LTL carrier’s North American terminal count reaches 300 

 Todd Maiden 

· Thursday, October 01, 2026 

 XPO expanded its North American footprint to 300 terminals following the addition of new service centers in Missouri and Arizona. (Photo: Jim Allen/FreightWaves) 

Less-than-truckload carrier XPO announced Thursday that it has added new locations in Arizona and Missouri, increasing its terminal count to 300 across North America.

A new 51,000-square-foot facility in Mesa, Arizona has 86 dock doors and over 100 employees. The terminal gives XPO (NYSE: XPO) needed capacity to serve the Phoenix market, where it already operates a freight assembly center. The region is experiencing an increase in demand given recent industrial investments and growing cross-border trade with Mexico.

A 13,000-square-foot terminal in Cameron, Missouri (approximately 50 miles north of Kansas City) has 32 dock doors and over 30 employees. It sits near the intersection of I-35 and U.S. 36, serving both north-south and east-west freight corridors.

# 3PL Arvato opens its seventh logistics facility in Louisville 

400,000 square foot site takes Arvato’s total Louisville footprint beyond four million square feet.

By DC Velocity Staff Oct 05, 2026

DC Velocity Staff See Full Bio 

The supply chain management and e-commerce third party logistics provider (3PL) Arvato has opened its seventh logistics facility in Louisville, Kentucky, saying the move further expands its presence in one of the United States’ most important logistics hubs.

The new, wholly-owned site adds approximately 400,000 square feet of capacity, taking Arvato’s total Louisville footprint beyond four million square feet. Expected to create approximately 150 new jobs, the facility further strengthens the company’s ability to support growing fulfillment and distribution requirements for clients across North America, Arvato said.

According to Germany-based Arvato, brands need supply chain solutions that can support growth without adding complexity, whether they are entering new markets, managing rising order volumes, or optimizing delivery performance.
